defects.proof: CPython pathlib: Path.is_file() catches OSError internally and returns False - it NEVER raises PermissionError. The new try/except OSError around present=path.is_file() is therefore dead: on POSIX chmod-0 dir, is_file() returns False -> STATUS_MISSING card, and the test assert reason_code==STATUS_UNREADABLE should FAIL on that path. Author claims green (20 passed) - irreconcilable unless (a) tests ran as root (chmod-0 ignored -> is_file True -> corrupt-journal path yields UNREADABLE for the wrong reason), or (b) the real EACCES surface is the journal read in the unseen second try. Either way the guard is on the wrong call and the test premise is wrong. Additionally chmod-0 is POSIX-only (Windows: read-only flag, still readable; root/admin immune) -> CI-portability hazard.
